full_judgment:
3. Respondent No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 11 of 2001 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Singair, Manikganj for declaration that R.S. record was wrong and also for partition contending, inter-alia, that the suit land belonged to Rashu Pramanik and others. Aditya Pramanik was the tenant under them. Aditya being in possession died leaving behind five sons named Lalit, Mahesh, Krishna, Puma and Gadadhar. C.S. Khatian No. 1356 was correctly prepared in their names. Out of the need for money 5(five) brothers gave 29 decimals of land to Nepal Bepary by korfa pattan. Lalit having died, Paresh Chandra Sarkar, son of Puma Chandra Sarkar got saham of the said 29 decimals of land upon amicable partition. Paresh tried to dispossess Nepal by denying his Korfa pattan. Thereafter, through the settlement of well wishers Paresh executed a kabala on 05.05.1955 but he without registering the same came back and ultimately, the deed was registered through miscellaneous case by presenting the same before the District Registrar. S.A. record was correctly prepared in the name of Nepal but R.S. record was not correctly prepared reflecting his actual share. Nepal died leaving behind two sons, defendant Nos. 1 and 2. Defendant No. 2 sold 8 decimals of land by a registered kabala dated 06.04.1982 to Gadadhar and Kalipada who mutated their names and paid rent. Thereafter, Gadadhar and Kalipada sold 7 decimals of land out of 8 decimals of land to the plaintiff by registered kabala dated 30.06.1992. Defendant No.1 transferred 6 decimals of land to the plaintiff by a kabala dated 30.12.1990. Gadadhar and Kalipada transferred decimal of land to the plaintiff. Though kabala was not registered, possession of the transferred land was handed over. This way the plaintiff is in possession of 14 decimals of land. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 possess their remaining 15 decimals of land through the plaintiff. The plaintiff sold 4 decimals of land to defendant No.10. The plaintiff has constructed a homestead on the suit land. The defendant having preferred appeal against the mutation order passed in favour of the plaintiff, revenue authority refused to take rent from the plaintiff, hence the, suit. 

 4. The present petitioner as defendant No.3 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the land of plot No.2015 under D.S. Khatian No.1356 belonged to Lalit, Mahesh,  Krishna, Puma Chandra and Gadadhar Pramanik. Gadadhar died bachelor leaving behind 4(four) brothers. Lalit being in possession of 1912 decimals of land; through amicable settlement died leaving behind his daughter Bhaganya Sundary and daughter's sons, namely, Bhim, Gokul and Haridas who being in possession of the land left by Lalit transferred the same by kabala dated 22.02.1955 in favour of Satish Chandra and Nani Gopal Sarkar. Krishna being in possession of 1412 decimals of land died leaving behind Laxmi Bewa, a widow who sold the said land to Fani Bhushan by a kabala dated 14.09.1970. Fani Bhushan transferred the said land to defendant No.3 by a kabala dated 11.04.1974. Punta Chandra died leaving behind a son, Paresh Chandra Sarkar, as his heir who transferred 10 decimals of land by a kabala dated 17.05.1955 in favour of Satish Chandra Sarkar. Mahesh died leaving behind two sons, namely, Kalipada and Mahedeb. The mother of Kalipada and Mahadeb transferred 1912 decimals of land which they got by amicable partition on behalf of her sons by a kabala dated 24.02.1955 in favour of Satish Chandra and Nani Gopal. Nani Gopal used to possess 16 decimals of land by amicable partition and he transferred 16 decimals of land in favour of defendant No.3 by a registered deed of gift. Satish died leaving behind his only son defendant No.3. This way defendant No.3 became the owner of 58 decimals of land in the suit plot and he is in possession thereof. The plaintiff is neither in possession nor has got any title in the suit property. All the claims of the plaintiff in this regard are false and as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 III. Whether the plaintiff was entitled to get saham in the suit land without establishing his title when his title therein was very much clouded because of the wrong recording of R.S. khatian.
